explanations.name: Rating
explanations.text: The rating is a mean-reversion trigger score from the 3 voting indicators (Bollinger, Stochastic, RSI): +1/-1 = Lean Buy/Lean Sell, +2/-2 = Buy/Sell, +3/-3 = Strong Buy/Strong Sell, 0 = Hold. Trend (50/200 EMA) is shown next to the rating as context but does NOT vote — otherwise a dip to oversold would always be cancelled out by the downtrend votes and everything would read Hold.

explanations.name: 50 EMA
explanations.text: Medium-term trend context (~10 weeks) — shown, not counted in the score. Price above = uptrend. Price below = downtrend. Reacts faster than the 200 EMA — useful for catching trend changes earlier.

explanations.name: 200 EMA
explanations.text: Long-term trend context (~40 weeks) — shown, not counted in the score. The institutional bull/bear benchmark. When the 50 EMA is above the 200 EMA the rating shows 'golden cross' (bullish regime); below shows 'death cross'. A downtrend raises the bar for buying a dip (falling-knife risk).

explanations.name: Bollinger Bands
explanations.text: Measures price relative to a 20-day volatility range (±2 std deviations). Near lower band = oversold, price cheap vs recent range. Mid-range = neutral. Near upper band = overbought, price stretched. Mean reversion signal — extreme readings suggest a move back toward the middle.

explanations.name: RSI
explanations.text: Momentum gauge — measures the speed of recent gains vs losses. Votes on absolute levels: below 30 = oversold (buy vote), above 70 = overbought (sell vote), in between = neutral. Whether RSI is rising or falling vs its own 14-day average is shown in brackets as momentum context but doesn't vote.

explanations.name: Stochastic
explanations.text: Where today's close sits within the 14-day high-low range. Below 20 = oversold, price near recent lows. 20-80 = neutral. Above 80 = overbought, price near recent highs. In a strong downtrend, can stay below 20 for weeks — oversold doesn't always mean imminent bounce.

explanations.name: Structure Rule
explanations.text: Gate on priority alerts only — doesn't affect the batch report score. For a buy alert: current bar must close higher AND make a higher low vs the prior bar. For a sell alert: lower close AND lower high. Blocks dead-cat bounces (higher close but lower low) and false breakouts.

explanations.name: Priority Alert
explanations.text: Fires when at least 2 of the 3 mean-reversion indicators agree the stock is oversold or overbought (trigger score >= +2 or <= -2) AND the structure rule confirms the bounce/rollover has started. This is the buy-low/sell-high entry signal.
